layers.title: Steep ground
layers.process: Mean heights on a ~2 m grid, smoothed 3x3 (~6 m baseline); slope from central differences. Yellow 15-25 deg, red > 25 deg.
caveats: Checked at 79 Perseverance positions: slope minus rover-measured tilt +0.6 deg median, 1.9 deg mean error. Map height minus rover height +0.00 m median (rover heights likely use the same map, so this shows agreement only).
layers.attribution: Derived by Baroler from the HiRISE DEM (Mars Trek)

layers.title: Routing grid
layers.process: 2 m heights, slope (whole degrees) and roughness (cm) used by the route finder and the radio check.
layers.attribution: Derived by Baroler from the HiRISE DEM (Mars Trek)

layers.title: Rock types (USGS SIM 3464)
layers.process: Units clipped and reprojected from the SIM 3464 geodatabase; drawn as an image. Vector shapes for look-ups: geology/units.geojson.
layers.attribution: Sun, V.Z., and Stack, K.M., 2020, USGS SIM 3464 (public domain)
caveats: Rock-type borders may be 100-200 m off (USGS SIM 3464 readme).

layers.title: Weather measured here (Perseverance MEDA)

values.meaning: air and ground temperature, pressure; sunrise and sunset

layers.process: Daily min/max and hourly medians over sols 1210-1218. Sunrise/sunset computed with Mars24 equations (checked: within 0.6 min of the rover's feed; equation of time within 0.08 min of MEDA's clocks).
caveats: Reference conditions from Jul 2024, when Perseverance was here; not today's weather.

layers.title: Sun activity (NOAA GOES)

values.meaning: solar flares (7 days) and >=10 MeV proton level (3 days)

caveats: GOES satellites near Earth (1 AU). Mars is about 1.5 AU from the Sun and often on another side, so storms seen here may or may not reach Mars.
NASA DONKI (S3): unreachable at build time.

site.name: Bright Angel (zone Z2)
site.description: Walk area around the Cheyava Falls rock, where Perseverance worked in mid-2024.

objectives.title: Study the spotted rocks at Cheyava Falls
objectives.question: Do the small dark spots in the Cheyava Falls rock hold signs of ancient life?
objectives.whyHumans: A geologist can look at the spots from many angles, compare nearby rocks, and choose the best sample on the spot.

objectives.title: Understand the rocks around Bright Angel
objectives.question: How do the rocks along the walk differ from the Cheyava Falls rock?
objectives.whyHumans: Walking between outcrops lets a person see how the layers connect.

assumptions.statement: Comfortable walking slope for a suited astronaut
Maximum slope allowed on foot (steeper = no-go)
Walking speed on flat ground in a suit
assumptions.reference: Speed on slopes scaled with Tobler's hiking function

assumptions.statement: Time kept in reserve for the walk back
Habitat position chosen by the planner: flat ground with the best radio view of the walk; not a real landing site
Habitat radio antenna height above ground
Suit radio antenna height above ground
Longest time allowed without radio contact to the habitat
Start the walk at least this long after sunrise
Be back at least this long before sunset
Postpone the walk if the 10 MeV proton level reaches this (NOAA S1 storm level, measured near Earth)
Take extra care for this long after an X-class solar flare
